ev.q: Considering EIP as the reference, sensitivity and positive predictive value of NNDSS were 78% (94 of 120) and 92% (94 of 102)
Completeness of information on major HCV infection risk factors ranged from 15% to 46% for NNDSS, compared with 70% to 77% in EIP sites.
The mean duration between diagnosis and reporting of the cases to the state health department was 30 days (range: 0--298 days) in NNDSS
Reporting of acute hepatitis C in routine national surveillance missed approximately 22% of cases
Presence or absence of jaundice was reported in 63% of cases from NNDSS and 98% of cases reported from EIP.
Evaluation of Acute Hepatitis C Infection Surveillance

methods_quotes.q: Sensitivity and positive predictive value of NNDSS for reporting acute hepatitis C cases were calculated
Timeliness of case reporting was based on calculating the interval between the date of diagnosis
CDC evaluated data quality by measuring the completeness of information on demographic and clinical variables
Cases reported to NNDSS and EIP were matched by a common case identifier and date of birth.
